prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1131; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of a sideswipe collision during a lane change on a multi-lane roadway. Insured vehicle contacted the left rear quarter panel of the claimant's vehicle. Both drivers reported they were stopped at the scene and exchanged information. Scene photos requested from insured.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. Claimant reports neck strain with stiffness and headaches since the impact and has not yet seen a physician. Claimant states they are not represented by an attorney and prefers to handle the claim directly. Advised claimant of medical evaluation options and asked for provider details once treatment begins.

Entry 3: Reviewed photos submitted by insured. Visible damage to the rear driver-side door and bumper cover on the claimant's vehicle, with scuffing consistent with a glancing contact. Insured's statement confirms the claimant's vehicle was in the adjacent lane and the insured failed to check the blind spot before merging. Liability appears to rest with the insured.

Entry 4: Claimant sent copy of urgent care visit notes diagnosing acute neck strain and recommending physical therapy and over-the-counter anti-inflammatories. Records reviewed and added to file. Requested itemized bills and any prior neck or back treatment history for the past several years.

Entry 5: Sent written estimate to claimant for repair of the rear quarter panel and door, with a copy to the body shop of their choice. Bodily injury evaluation remains open pending completion of physical therapy and a follow-up report from the treating provider. Claimant informed of next steps and of the right to request a review if they disagree with any part of the settlement position.
